what: MSCI sells investment indexes and analytics. Fund managers pay to track its indexes, such as MSCI World and MSCI Emerging Markets, and institutions pay for its risk models, private asset data and sustainability ratings.
customers: Asset managers, exchange-traded fund providers, pension funds, banks, insurers and hedge funds.
money: licence fees on funds tracking its indexes and subscription data
ESG and climate ratings and data
moat: Indexes written into fund mandates and benchmarks, so changing provider means changing what a fund is contractually obliged to track.
risks: Index revenue rises and falls with the assets tracking its indexes, so a market fall cuts revenue
Debt of about $7 billion against very little cash
Passive fund fee pressure flows through to index licensing rates
European sustainability regulation has shifted demand for ESG data
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 37% and a 55% operating margin
Subscription revenue renews at very high rates
Private asset data is a newer market where it has been buying capability
watch: Assets under management linked to its indexes and the retention rate on subscriptions.
